subject.title: [Architecture] Decouple audio processing pipeline from core speech bindings in packages/speech-core

question: Should OpenClaw support a separately consumable metadata-only speech package, or should native-dependency reduction remain an internal build/package optimization?
rationale: The issue asks for a public package-boundary change but supplies no demonstrated external consumer contract or evidence that the current package layout causes a user-facing install burden.

options.title: Request a scoped design and proof
options.body: Require a dependency trace, affected consumer scenario, proposed import contract, and compatibility plan before accepting a package split.

options.title: Treat as internal optimization
options.body: Keep the existing package API and pursue any dependency reduction only as an owner-led build optimization without promising a new package surface.

options.title: Decline the split for now
options.body: Leave the current boundary intact unless a supported consumer demonstrates a concrete install or runtime problem.

recommendation.title: Request a scoped design and proof
recommendation.body: Require a dependency trace, affected consumer scenario, proposed import contract, and compatibility plan before accepting a package split.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent public speech-core ownership analysis makes this the strongest available routing signal.
